text:
Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed set of nodes (the reservoir) that are randomly connected and have their weights set during training. The reservoir's state is then used to map the input data, and a simple linear layer is trained on top to make predictions. Training typically involves adjusting the readout weights, while the reservoir's weights remain fixed.
